   # 'emithls' Dialect
   
   The `emithls` dialect groups together a set of types, operations and
   transformations that are useful to represent a High-Level Synthese
   style C++ code.
   These abstractions works as a.
   
   [TOC]

   ### `emithls.expr` (emithls::ExpressionOp)
   
   _Represents a combined C/C++ expression._
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   operation ::= `emithls.expr` attr-dict `:` type($result) $body
   ```
   
   The `expression` operation defines a set of operations that together
   form a C/C++ style complex expression, such as:
   `int var = (a + b) * c;`.
   This operation returns one value with a scalar type, which is yielded
   from the region using `YieldOp`.
   Nested expressions are also allowed.
   Example:
   ```
   // Assume %lhs, %rhs, %cst are i32 values
   %expr = emithls.expr : i32 {
       %0 = arith.addi %lhs, %cst : i32
       %1 = arith.muli %0, %rhs : i32
       emithls.yield %1 : i32
   }
   ```
   
   Traits: `NoRegionArguments`, `SingleBlockImplicitTerminator<YieldOp>`, `SingleBlock`
   
   Interfaces: `OpAsmOpInterface`
   
   #### Results:
   
   | Result | Description |
   | :----: | ----------- |
   | `result` | any non-token type |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.for` (emithls::ForOp)
   
   _Defines a C/C++ for loop._
   
   The `for` operation defines a counted loop with compile-time constant
   lower bound, upper bound, and step, mapping to a C/C++ `for` loop.
   The loop body receives the current induction variable as a block
   argument and iterates from `lowerBound` to `upperBound` (exclusive)
   in increments of `step`.
   Example:
   ```
   emithls.for %idx0 = 0 to 10 step 1 {
       ops using %idx0 ...
   }
   ```
   
   Traits: `NoTerminator`, `RecursiveMemoryEffects`
   
   Interfaces: `OpAsmOpInterface`
   
   #### Attributes:
   
   <table>
   <tr><th>Attribute</th><th>MLIR Type</th><th>Description</th></tr>
   <tr><td><code>lowerBound</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>index attribute</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>upperBound</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>index attribute</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>step</code></td><td>::mlir::IntegerAttr</td><td>index attribute</td></tr>
   </table>
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.func` (emithls::FuncOp)
   
   _Defines a C/C++ function with a void return type._
   
   The `func` operation defines a C/C++ function with a void return type,
   serving as the node and top-level function unit for HLS code generation.
   The function is identified by its symbol name and is isolated from
   above, meaning it cannot reference values defined outside its scope.
   Function arguments are accessible via the entry block of the body region.
   Example:
   ```
   emithls.func @my_func(%arg0: type, %arg1: type, ...) {
       ops...
   }
   ```
   
   Traits: `AutomaticAllocationScope`, `IsolatedFromAbove`, `NoTerminator`
   
   Interfaces: `ArgAndResultAttrsOpInterface`, `CallableOpInterface`, `FunctionOpInterface`, `Symbol`
   
   #### Attributes:
   
   <table>
   <tr><th>Attribute</th><th>MLIR Type</th><th>Description</th></tr>
   <tr><td><code>sym_name</code></td><td>::mlir::StringAttr</td><td>string attribute</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>function_type</code></td><td>::mlir::TypeAttr</td><td>type attribute of function type</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>arg_attrs</code></td><td>::mlir::ArrayAttr</td><td>Array of dictionary attributes</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>res_attrs</code></td><td>::mlir::ArrayAttr</td><td>Array of dictionary attributes</td></tr>
   </table>

   ### `emithls.if` (emithls::IfOp)
   
   _Defines a C/C style if-statement._
   
   The `if` operation conditionally executes one of two regions based on
   an `i1` condition value, mapping to a C/C++ `if`/`else` statement.
   The `then` region is always executed when the condition is true.
   The optional `else` region is executed when the condition is false;
   if absent, no action is taken on the false path.
   Example:
   ```
   emithls.if %cond {
       ops ...
   } else {
       ops ...
   }
   ```
   
   Traits: `NoRegionArguments`, `NoTerminator`, `RecursiveMemoryEffects`
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `condition` | 1-bit signless integer |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.include` (emithls::IncludeOp)
   
   _C/C++ include statement_
   
   The `include` operation abstracts the C/C++ include syntax.
   However, this operation does not check the existence of the
   header file.
   This operation is created automatically by a transformation pass
   inside this dialect.
   
   Traits: `HasParent<ModuleOp>`
   
   #### Attributes:
   
   <table>
   <tr><th>Attribute</th><th>MLIR Type</th><th>Description</th></tr>
   <tr><td><code>header</code></td><td>::mlir::StringAttr</td><td>string attribute</td></tr>
   </table>

   ### `emithls.stream.read` (emithls::StreamReadOp)
   
   _Reads data out from hls::stream._
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   operation ::= `emithls.stream.read` $stream (`[` $indices^ `]`)? attr-dict `:` qualified(type($stream)) `->` type($data)
   ```
   
   Interfaces: `MemoryEffectsOpInterface`
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `stream` | Stream type in HLS C++ or Array type in C++ |
   | `indices` | variadic of index |
   
   #### Results:
   
   | Result | Description |
   | :----: | ----------- |
   | `data` | any non-token type |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.stream.write` (emithls::StreamWriteOp)
   
   _Writes data into hls::stream._
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   operation ::= `emithls.stream.write` $data `to` $stream (`[` $indices^ `]`)? attr-dict `:` type($data) `->` qualified(type($stream))
   ```
   
   Interfaces: `MemoryEffectsOpInterface`
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `data` | any non-token type |
   | `stream` | Stream type in HLS C++ or Array type in C++ |
   | `indices` | variadic of index |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.top_interface` (emithls::PragmaTopInterfaceOp)
   
   _#pragma HLS INTERFACE for the top function_
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   operation ::= `emithls.top_interface` attr-dict
   ```
   
   Interfaces: `EmitHLS_PragmaInterface`
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.update` (emithls::UpdateOp)
   
   _Defines a C/C++ style assignment._
   
   The `update` operation performs a C/C++ style assignment to an
   existing variable.
   This operation also supports element-wise assignment for array
   types using a list of `IndexType` indices.
   ```
   emithls.update %var with %new_value : type <- type
   emithls.update %var with %arr[%indices]
       : type <- !emithls.array<shape x type>
   emithls.update %arr[%indices] with %new_value
       : !emithls.array<shape x type> <- type
   emithls.update %arr0[%indices] with %arr1[%indices]
       : !emithls.array<shape x type> <- !emithls.array<shape x type>
   ```
   
   Traits: `AttrSizedOperandSegments`
   
   Interfaces: `MemoryEffectsOpInterface`
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `variable` | any non-token type |
   | `indices` | variadic of index |
   | `new_value` | any non-token type |
   | `new_value_indices` | variadic of index |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.variable` (emithls::VariableOp)
   
   _Defines a C/C++ style variable._
   
   The `variable` operation defines a C/C++ variable, which is used to
   simplify the translation from `emithls` dialect to HLS code.
   MLIR adopts the Single Static Assignment form, which forbids multiple
   assignments to the same variable.
   To solve this, the `variable` operation and an `update` operation are
   defined, such as:
   ```
   %var = emithls.variable : type
   emithls.update %var, %value : type
   ```
   A `variable` can also be defined as a constant as in C/C++.
   
   Interfaces: `OpAsmOpInterface`
   
   #### Attributes:
   
   <table>
   <tr><th>Attribute</th><th>MLIR Type</th><th>Description</th></tr>
   <tr><td><code>init_number</code></td><td>::mlir::Attribute</td><td>any attribute</td></tr>
   <tr><td><code>is_const</code></td><td>::mlir::UnitAttr</td><td>unit attribute</td></tr>
   </table>
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `init_value` | any non-token type |
   
   #### Results:
   
   | Result | Description |
   | :----: | ----------- |
   | `variable` | any non-token type |
   
   
   
   ### `emithls.yield` (emithls::YieldOp)
   
   _Yields the result value of an expression._
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   operation ::= `emithls.yield` attr-dict $value `:` type($value)
   ```
   
   The `yield` operation terminates an expression block with a value,
   which becomes the result of the enclosing expression.
   This operation mimics a combined expression in C/C++.
   
   Traits: `AlwaysSpeculatableImplTrait`, `HasParent<ExpressionOp>`, `Terminator`
   
   Interfaces: `ConditionallySpeculatable`, `NoMemoryEffect (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`
   
   Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{}`
   
   #### Operands:
   
   | Operand | Description |
   | :-----: | ----------- |
   | `value` | any non-token type |
   
   
   
   ## Attributes
   
   ### DenseFixedAttr
   
   _Constant densely-packed array of fixed-point values_
   
   The `dense_fixed` attribute represents a compile-time constant array
   of values that each define the value of a common `FixedType` element
   type.
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   dense-fixed-attr ::= `dense_fixed` `<` $type `=` $data `>`
   ```
   
   The result type must be a statically-shaped `ArrayType` of `FixedType`
   elements, and the dense elements contained must match the shape of
   type, or be a splat.
   
   Example:
   
   ```
   #emithls.dense_fixed<!emithls.array<3x!emithls.fixed<4, 2>> = dense<[1, 2, 3]>>
   ```
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | type | `::mlir::Type` |  |
   | data | `DenseIntElementsAttr` |  |
   
   ### FixedAttr
   
   _Constant fixed-point bit-pattern attribute_
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   #emithls.fixed<
     ::mlir::Type,   # type
     ::mlir::base2::BitSequence   # value
   >
   ```
   
   The `fixed` attribute represents a compile-time constant bit pattern
   that defines the value of a `FixedType`.
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   fixed-attr   ::= `fixed` `<` bit-sequence `>` `:` type
   bit-sequence ::= `"` bit-literal (trunc-spec)? `"`
   bit-literal  ::= `0b` [_01]* | `0x` [_0-9a-fA-F]*
   trunc-spec   ::= `/` [0-9]+
   ```
   
   The number of bits in the bit-sequence must equal the type's total
   bit width.
   
   Example:
   
   ```
   #emithls.fixed<"0b0100"> : !emithls.fixed<4, 2>
   ```
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | type | `::mlir::Type` |  |
   | value | `::mlir::base2::BitSequence` |  |
   
   ## Types
   
   ### ArrayType
   
   _Array type in C++_
   
   The `array` type represents a C++ style array, which contains
   a shaped amount of variables of one scalar type, such as:
   `!emithls.array<2xi32>`, `!emithls.array<2x2xi32>`
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | shape | `::llvm::ArrayRef<int64_t>` |  |
   | elementType | `Type` |  |
   
   ### FixedType
   
   _AP_Fixed type in HLS C++_
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   !emithls.fixed<
     int64_t,   # totalBits
     int64_t   # intBits
   >
   ```
   
   The `fixed` type represents a HLS C++ `ap_fixed<totalBits, intBits>`
   fixed-point number. `totalBits` is the overall bit width and `intBits`
   is the number of integer bits, which includes the sign bit. The
   number of fractional bits is implicit: `totalBits - intBits`.
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | totalBits | `int64_t` |  |
   | intBits | `int64_t` |  |
   
   ### PointerType
   
   _Pointer type in HLS C++_
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   !emithls.ptr<
     Type   # elementType
   >
   ```
   
   The `pointer` type represents a C++ pointer type, which points
   to the address of a value, e.g. `!emithls.ptr<i32>`.
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | elementType | `Type` |  |
   
   ### StreamType
   
   _Stream type in HLS C++_
   
   Syntax:
   
   ```
   !emithls.stream<
     Type   # elementType
   >
   ```
   
   The `stream` type represents a HLS C++ hls::stream type, which
   constructs an FIFO stream with element type flowing in it,
   e.g. `!emithls.stream<i32>`.
   
   #### Parameters:
   
   | Parameter | C++ type | Description |
   | :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
   | elementType | `Type` |  |
